courses.fullname: Vyaapaar - Key Roles and Responsibilities of Area Sales Manager
courses.displayname: Vyaapaar - Key Roles and Responsibilities of Area Sales Manager
courses.summary: The training module on Roles and Responsibilities of an Area Sales Manager provides valuable insights into the crucial aspects of this role. Starting with a productive morning routine, the Area Sales Manager sets the tone for the day by communicating commitments and discussing the agenda with the Cluster Head. The module emphasizes the importance of face-to-face interactions, with a minimum of five visits per day, including two visits before 11 am. Onboarding and activating new retailers are key responsibilities, along with achieving monthly targets by selling devices or onboarding new Distributors and Super-Distributors. Building relationships with existing merchants and re-engaging inactive merchants are vital for sustainable business growth. Collaborative meetings and active participation in drives, schemes, and contests foster teamwork and success. Engaging with newly launched products and transparent reporting ensure market competitiveness and accountability. The Area Sales Manager is also responsible for expanding the distribution network and focusing on onboarding, One Time Revenue (OTR), and Gross Transaction Value (GTV) targets. By implementing these strategies and focusing on customer-centric approaches, ASMs can drive sales and contribute to organizational success.

The course also covers transactional tools and risk management practices essential for BCs to facilitate secure and efficient financial transactions. Additionally, it equips learners with the basics of selling techniques and emphasizes the significance of accounting and settlement processes in maintaining financial transparency. Moreover, the course underscores the pivotal role of customer service in building trust and fostering financial literacy among customers, showcasing the range of apps provided by banks to BCs to enhance their service delivery capabilities and streamline operations. Overall, the course empowers BCs with the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively serve as intermediaries in expanding financial access and promoting inclusive growth.

This comprehensive course provides a foundational and in-depth exploration of the Indian banking system, designed for students, professionals, and anyone seeking to understand the financial backbone of the world's fastest-growing major economy.

The course is structured to take you on a journey from the basic principles of banking to the complex, multi-layered structure of India's financial ecosystem. You will gain a clear understanding of how banks function, their pivotal role in economic development, and how they impact everyday life.

Key Learning Objectives:

Upon completion of this course, you will be able to:

  • Explain the fundamental concepts and core functions of banking, including deposit acceptance, lending, and payment systems.

  • Map the complete structure of the Indian banking system, differentiating between Scheduled and Non-Scheduled Banks, and understanding the roles of Public Sector, Private Sector, Foreign, Cooperative, and Regional Rural Banks.

  • Understand the pivotal role and functions of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the central bank, including monetary policy, regulation, currency management, and financial stability.

  • Identify and compare the various types of bank accounts available in India (e.g., Savings, Current, FDs, RDs, Demat, NRI accounts) and determine which are suited for different needs.

  • Trace the historical evolution of Indian banking from its colonial roots through nationalization and liberalization to the current digital revolution.

  • Analyze the impact of key government initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) and Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) on financial inclusion and economic growth.

  • Evaluate the transformative impact of technology on banking, with a special focus on India's globally acclaimed Unified Payments Interface (UPI), digital wallets, and the future of banking with AI, Blockchain, and Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC).

Core Modules Covered:

  1. Introduction to Banking: The role of banks as financial intermediaries, their core services, and their impact on individuals and the economy.

  2. Banking's Economic Role: How banks facilitate economic growth, ensure financial stability, and promote savings and investments.

  3. Banking Functions & Services: A detailed look at the services banks offer, from loans and payments to wealth management and insurance.

  4. Structure & Regulation: An in-depth study of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and its functions as the regulator and guardian of the financial system.

  5. Types of Banks in India: A complete breakdown of the different layers of banks, including Commercial, Cooperative, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, and Payments Banks.

  6. Bank Accounts in India: A practical guide to the diverse range of accounts available, from basic savings to specialized accounts for businesses, NRIs, and investors.

  7. Evolution & Future of Banking: A historical journey from pre-independence to the digital age, analyzing past challenges, current trends, and future directions like Open Banking and AI.

Who is this course for?

  • Students of finance, economics, and business management.

  • Early-career professionals in banking and financial services.

  • Entrepreneurs and business owners seeking to understand financing.

  • Any individual looking to make informed personal financial decisions and enhance their financial literacy.

This course equips you with the essential knowledge to navigate the Indian financial landscape with confidence, whether you are opening your first bank account, seeking a business loan, or simply aiming to understand the forces that drive the Indian economy.

courses.fullname: Various Deposit Schemes and other Services
courses.displayname: Various Deposit Schemes and other Services
courses.summary:
This course provides a comprehensive understanding of modern banking deposit schemes and related financial services, equipping learners with the knowledge to make informed, strategic financial decisions. Designed for students and professionals alike, it explores how different deposit options serve individuals and institutions across life stages and financial goals.

Learners will begin by examining the fundamental role of deposits in the banking ecosystem—how they fuel the economy and support personal financial security. Through detailed modules, the course dives into the core deposit products offered by banks: Savings Accounts, Fixed Deposits (FDs), and Recurring Deposits (RDs)—explaining their structures, benefits, interest mechanisms, and practical applications through real-life examples and case studies.

Building on this foundation, the course introduces specialized deposit schemes such as Senior Citizen Savings Schemes (SCSS), Tax-Saver FDs, Minor Accounts, and NRI Deposit Options (NRE, NRO, and FCNR accounts). Learners will understand how these schemes align with specific needs such as tax planning, retirement income, child savings, or managing foreign earnings.

The course also highlights the integration of digital banking innovations—including online account management, automated deposit features, and AI-based financial tools—transforming traditional banking into a customer-centric digital experience.

In its concluding modules, learners explore other essential banking services that complement deposit products, including overdrafts, joint accounts, insurance protection, and regulatory safeguards like deposit insurance. Interactive quizzes and case analyses reinforce key concepts, ensuring learners gain both conceptual clarity and practical insight.

courses.fullname: Account Opening, on-Boarding Process, KYC Mechanism and Operations
courses.displayname: Account Opening, on-Boarding Process, KYC Mechanism and Operations
courses.summary:
This course provides an in-depth understanding of the bank account opening and onboarding process, focusing on the Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) framework as mandated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

Learners will gain practical knowledge of the step-by-step procedure for opening different types of accounts, including Aadhaar-based account opening, along with the importance of collecting photographs, specimen signatures, and nomination details to ensure compliance and customer security.

The course also explains the principles of KYC and AML, highlighting RBI’s regulatory guidelines and the role of banking representatives in preventing money laundering and safeguarding the integrity of the financial system. Finally, learners will understand the correct procedures for account closure, ensuring smooth and compliant operations from start to finish.

By the end of this course, participants will be able to confidently assist customers through every stage of the account lifecycle—from opening to closure—while upholding compliance, transparency, and trust.

courses.fullname: Grievance Redressal Mechanism in Banks and Banking Ombudsman Scheme.
courses.displayname: Grievance Redressal Mechanism in Banks and Banking Ombudsman Scheme.
courses.summary:
This course offers a clear and practical understanding of how customer grievances are handled in the Indian banking system. It explains the internal grievance redressal process of banks, including complaint lodging channels, resolution timelines, and escalation levels, along with the role of the Internal Ombudsman (IO) in ensuring fair review of unresolved complaints.

Learners will also understand the RBI’s Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021, covering when and how customers can approach the RBI Ombudsman, the filing process, and the decision-making framework. Real-life case studies illustrate how issues such as wrong charges, ATM disputes, and service failures are resolved.

By the end, learners will be equipped to guide customers effectively, ensure timely grievance handling, and strengthen trust through transparent, RBI-compliant practices.

courses.fullname: Financial Inclusion and Banking for the Unbanked
courses.displayname: Financial Inclusion and Banking for the Unbanked
courses.summary:
This course introduces learners to the concept of financial inclusion, the challenges faced by India’s unbanked population, and the national initiatives designed to bring them into the formal financial system. It explores key drivers such as PMJDY, social security schemes, and the transformative role of India Stack—Aadhaar, e-KYC, UPI, and mobile banking—reshaping access to financial services A major focus is the Business Correspondent (BC) model, which delivers doorstep banking in remote areas. Real case studies—like the Bank Sakhi in Bihar and Akodara’s digital village model—demonstrate how BCs, technology, and government programs are improving livelihoods and enabling secure savings, credit, insurance, and pension access for underserved groups .

By the end of the course, learners will understand India’s financial inclusion journey, barriers to inclusion, key government schemes, and practical strategies to extend banking services to every household—especially in rural and low-income communities.

courses.fullname: BC/BF Model:A Vehicle for Financial Inclusion
courses.displayname: BC/BF Model:A Vehicle for Financial Inclusion
courses.summary:
This course provides an in-depth understanding of the Business Correspondent (BC) and Business Facilitator (BF) model, one of India’s most powerful frameworks for extending banking and financial services to underserved and remote populations. Learners will explore the structure, functions, regulatory foundations, and operational guidelines governing BCs and BFs, along with the roles each plays in enabling inclusive, accessible, and technology-driven banking.

The course covers the RBI guidelines, eligibility norms, distance criteria, onboarding processes, risk controls, and the “Do’s and Don’ts” that ensure transparency and trust at the last mile. It also explains the partnership ecosystem between banks, BC agents, customer service points, and technology providers—highlighting how digital tools such as Aadhaar-enabled biometrics, micro-ATMs, AEPS, and e-KYC power efficient service delivery.

A key component of the course is the set of real-life success stories, such as the PMJDY “Bank Mitra” movement, the BC Sakhi model empowering women through decentralized banking, and the transformation of rural access during major events like demonetization, COVID-19, and DBT rollouts. These case studies illustrate how BCs and BFs act as trusted financial intermediaries, crisis responders, and digital enablers in their communities.

By the end of the course, learners will understand:

  • The full operational framework of the BC/BF model

  • Roles, responsibilities, risk controls, and compliance requirements

  • Technology and digital processes used in last-mile banking

  • How BCs help expand savings, credit, insurance, and government benefit delivery

  • How success stories across India demonstrate the model’s power in driving financial empowerment

This course equips learners—especially aspiring or current BCs/BFs, banking staff, and financial inclusion practitioners—to deliver secure, reliable, and meaningful financial services in underserved regions, making them active partners in India’s financial inclusion revolution.

This course provides a deep understanding of fraud risk, its impact, and the systems used to prevent and detect fraud in banking. It covers RBI fraud classifications, digital fraud patterns, major real-life case studies, red-flag indicators, and core internal controls such as maker-checker, KYC integrity, Early Warning Systems, and transaction monitoring. Through detailed examples and regulatory guidelines, learners understand how frauds develop, how to identify vulnerabilities, and how strong processes, technology, and vigilance can protect customers, banks, and financial systems.

courses.fullname: Financial Inclusion and Social Security Schemes
courses.displayname: Financial Inclusion and Social Security Schemes
courses.summary: This course provides a clear understanding of India’s financial inclusion journey and the social security frameworks designed to protect low-income and unorganized-sector households. It explains how PMJDY, Aadhaar-enabled banking, and the BC/BF network have expanded access to savings, insurance, and pensions. Learners will explore the three major nationwide schemes—PMJJBY, PMSBY, and APY—covering their purpose, benefits, eligibility, and claim processes. The course also highlights the operational roles of banks and Business Correspondents in delivering these services and ensuring last-mile outreach. By the end, participants will be able to guide customers confidently and support meaningful, large-scale financial empowerment.

courses.fullname: Basic Technical Skills (handling Micro-ATMs, Biometric and other Devices, Basic Connectivity issues
courses.displayname: Basic Technical Skills (handling Micro-ATMs, Biometric and other Devices, Basic Connectivity issues
courses.summary:
This course equips learners with the essential technical skills required to confidently operate micro-ATMs, biometric scanners, and other banking service devices used in field operations. It covers the working process of micro-ATMs, their hardware components, Aadhaar-enabled authentication, and best-practice guidelines for delivering secure and seamless transactions in remote areas. Learners also gain hands-on understanding of biometric devices, including fingerprint capture techniques, resolving authentication failures, and maintaining device hygiene for accurate results.

The course further builds strong problem-solving skills to handle common connectivity issues—such as low network strength, intermittent signal drops, and transaction failures—along with practical steps to stabilize service delivery. In addition, participants learn general troubleshooting for card readers, printers, software glitches, power issues, and performance slowdowns, with clarity on when and how to escalate critical technical problems.

By the end of this training, learners are equipped to ensure smooth, secure, and uninterrupted customer service by applying effective device handling, connectivity management, and technical troubleshooting techniques essential for daily BC operations.

This course provides a complete understanding of India’s rapidly expanding digital banking ecosystem and the technologies that power modern financial services. Learners explore the full range of digital channels, including mobile banking, internet banking, SMS alerts, micro-ATMs, and interoperable payment systems such as UPI, AePS, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, RuPay, BBPS, and FASTag. The course explains how digital onboarding, e-KYC, Aadhaar-based verification, and video KYC have transformed customer acquisition and service delivery. Practical guidance is provided on secure usage of digital channels, data protection, password hygiene, and identifying fraud risks in real-world scenarios.
Participants also learn how Business Correspondents support customers in rural and semi-urban areas by facilitating digital transactions, educating users, and ensuring last-mile access to banking. Case-based demonstrations—such as live UPI flows, authentication journeys, and AePS transactions—help learners build strong operational clarity.
By the end of the course, learners gain a well-rounded understanding of the structure, functionality, and safe delivery of digital banking products, preparing them to support customers confidently and effectively.

Transform Customer Interactions from Challenging to Championed.

This comprehensive, skills-based course is meticulously designed for frontline professionals across retail, hospitality, healthcare, public service, and any customer-facing role. Move beyond theory and master a proven, practical framework to confidently engage with any customer personality, turning potential conflicts into opportunities for loyalty and trust.

Who Is This For?

This course is essential for frontline service professionals, sales associates, front desk agents, customer support representatives, bank officers, public service staff, and team leaders who are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences.

Enroll today and stop dreading difficult interactions—start mastering them. Equip yourself with the skills to not just serve customers, but to connect with them, ensuring every interaction ends on a positive note.

By the end of the course, IC members will be prepared to apply best practices immediately, strengthen organizational compliance, and contribute to building a safe, respectful, and legally compliant workplace culture.

courses.fullname: Understanding the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP)

Learners will gain a clear understanding of how Airpay enables seamless financial services through payment acceptance, disbursement, and business management solutions.

The course explores key entities including Airpay Vyaapaar, Airpay Fintech, Airpay UAE, Airpay Tanzania, Airpay Money, EMARS, and Airpay Academy—highlighting their roles, target audiences, and strategic contributions to financial inclusion and digital transformation.

Participants will also understand Airpay’s approach to embedded finance, API-driven infrastructure, and compliance-led operations, along with its focus on empowering underserved communities and enabling global payment ecosystems.

Additionally, the course introduces Airpay’s organizational values, global presence, customer segments, and policy frameworks that govern ethical conduct, inclusivity, and information security.

Welcome to our Comprehensive Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Course, where participants will gain a profound understanding of the multifaceted landscape of money laundering and the pivotal role played by Anti Money Laundering measures. This course is tailored for professionals within the financial industry, regulatory bodies, and individuals seeking to fortify financial systems against illicit activities. The curriculum commences with an exploration of the fundamental concept of money laundering, dissecting its historical context through a lens of notable cases that have shaped global financial systems. Participants will then delve into the intricate process of money laundering, with real-world examples illustrating each stage. The course further unravels the significance of Anti Money Laundering (AML), providing a comprehensive overview of the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2006, and its key provisions. Understanding the principles and objectives of AML, participants will navigate the global AML framework and regulatory landscape. Additionally, the course addresses vital topics such as KYC/AML policies for banks, customer due diligence, record-keeping, AML transaction monitoring, reporting of suspicious transactions, and the implementation of a risk-based approach. By the end of this course, participants will be well-equipped to contribute actively to the prevention and detection of money laundering activities in diverse financial environments.

The course covers essential topics, including the three pillars of IT security: confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Participants will learn about key security objectives, such as risk management, data encryption, password management, and email security best practices. The course also emphasizes the vital role employees play in maintaining security protocols, including identifying potential security risks, preventing unauthorized access, and protecting sensitive data.

By the end of this course, participants will be equipped with practical knowledge to contribute to a secure digital environment, effectively recognize and respond to potential threats, and support their organization’s efforts to prevent security breaches and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

courses.summary: This course explains the Auth, Capture, and Release payment workflow—a two-step card transaction process widely used in industries where final transaction amounts vary. Learners will understand how authorization blocks funds, how capture finalizes the payment, and how unused amounts are released back to customers. The course also covers real-world use cases, transaction lifecycle tracking in the Merchant Admin panel, and API-based execution.

This course introduces the Revalidation Flag mechanism used to resolve pending transactions where bank confirmation is delayed or missing. Learners will understand how reconciliation works, how decisions are made to credit merchants or refund customers, and how different revalidation rules impact transaction outcomes. The course also clarifies operational controls and the role of sales teams in configuring merchant preferences.

This course covers the Retry Flag feature designed to improve payment success rates by allowing customers to retry failed transactions without restarting the payment journey. Learners will understand how retry flows work, configuration controls within the Merchant Admin panel, and the impact on customer experience and conversion rates. The course also highlights the sales positioning of this feature.

This course explains how Branded Checkout enhances the payment experience by aligning the payment page with the merchant’s brand identity. Learners will explore when this feature is applicable, how it works in redirection-based integrations, and what customization options are available. The course also highlights its impact on customer trust, conversion rates, and sales positioning for brand-sensitive businesses.

This course introduces Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC), a feature that allows international customers to view and pay in their home currency during transactions. Learners will understand how DCC improves transparency, enhances customer experience, and increases conversion rates for global merchants. The course also covers pricing, markup logic, and end-to-end payment flow.

This course focuses on Dash Checkout, a streamlined checkout solution designed to reduce friction and improve conversion rates for eCommerce and D2C brands. Learners will understand how simplified checkout journeys, smart data prefill, and integrated logistics improve customer experience. The course also covers merchant-side benefits, integration simplicity, and its impact on business growth.

This course explains the Push to Merchant feature, a risk-control mechanism designed to prevent fraud and accidental payments in UPI static QR transactions. Learners will understand how settlement blocking works, how refunds are triggered, and why this feature is critical for small merchants using static QR codes. The course also covers real-world scenarios, limitations, and merchant education strategies.

This course provides a detailed understanding of Brand EMI, Airpay’s zero-cost EMI solution that enables merchants to boost high-value sales. Learners will explore how EMI interest is absorbed by merchants and refunded to customers, creating a true zero-interest experience. The course also covers customer journey, cost distribution, campaign setup, and effective sales positioning for different merchant segments.

This course explains Dynamic Split Settlement, a feature that automates the distribution of payments to multiple stakeholders based on predefined rules. Learners will understand how DSS eliminates manual reconciliation, reduces disputes, and enables scalable marketplace models. The course also covers configuration logic, use cases, and sales positioning for platform-based businesses.

This course introduces Instant Refund, a feature that enables near real-time refund processing for UPI transactions. Learners will understand how it improves customer experience, reduces complaints, and supports high-volume businesses. The course also covers activation flow, charges, operational steps, and best practices for positioning this feature to merchants.

This training on Phishing Awareness is designed to help employees understand and identify common fishing threats such as fake emails, messages, and calls. Through real-life examples and easy-to-follow tips, participants will learn how to recognize red flags, avoid clicking on suspicious links, and protect personal and company data. The session aims to build a strong foundation of cyber safety awareness for both work and personal life.
